record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.original_question: A preliminary comparison is said to connect parameters of the SK theory with those of Landau theory. Can the SK theory be reformulated in terms of modern theories of quantum phase transitions, so that its phase structure, control parameters, and predicted transitions are expressed using the language and methods of contemporary quantum critical phenomena rather than the original semiclassical presentation?

evidence.quote: A preliminary attempt in that direction has recently been performed in [21],where is was shown how the parameters appearing in the SK theory can be connected with those of the Landau theory. It would be interesting trying to reformulate the SK theory along the lines of present day theories of quantum phase transitions

artifact.category_tag: quantum phase transitions in dense matter
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the semiclassical (SK) theory of dense matter, formulated as an expansion of the many-body free energy functional F[ρ] in powers of ℏ around the Thomas–Fermi limit, with order parameters describing density inhomogeneities, pairing, or magnetic ordering in a strongly interacting fermion system at high density. Suppose that the parameters of this SK theory (e.g. gradient coefficients, effective coupling constants, and chemical-potential-dependent susceptibilities) have already been put into correspondence with those of a Landau-type free-energy expansion F_L[φ] = a(g) φ² + b φ⁴ + c (∇φ)² + … in an order parameter φ with a control parameter g.

Problem: Reformulate the SK theory within the framework of modern theories of quantum phase transitions. Concretely, identify
(i) a quantum order parameter field φ(x, τ) on d+1-dimensional space–time (with imaginary time τ ∈ [0, β]),
(ii) an effective quantum action S[φ] of Hertz–Millis type, including its dynamical exponent z, correlation-length exponent ν, and tuning parameter (e.g. density, pressure, or coupling) that drives the system through a quantum critical point at zero temperature,
(iii) the resulting phase diagram in the (T, g)-plane, including quantum critical, quantum disordered, and thermally disordered regimes,
such that the predictions of the SK theory for the phase structure of dense matter (locations of transitions, scaling of order parameters, and low-temperature thermodynamic anomalies) are reproduced by the universal scaling behavior of this quantum critical action.

State explicitly the dictionary between SK parameters and (a, b, c, g, z, ν), and determine the universality class of the implied quantum phase transition(s).
artifact.status_search_result: No specific published reformulation of the SK semiclassical theory of dense matter in the language of modern quantum phase transitions (Hertz–Millis type actions, dynamical exponents, quantum critical scaling) could be verified. The question appears to remain a programmatic open direction rather than a settled result.
